newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan trade surplus falls 12.9 percent in October.
newsitem.headline: Japan trade surplus falls 12.9 percent in October.

text.p: Japan's customs-cleared trade surplus fell 12.9 percent in October from a year ago to 470.86 billion yen, the 23rd consecutive month it has declined on a year-on-year basis, the Ministry of Finance Ministry said on Monday.
The surplus with the United States, often a source of trade friction, rose 31.3 percent to 354.79 billion yen in October from a year earlier. The figures were not adjusted for seasonal factors.
Japan's trade figures are released in yen. At Monday morning's dollar exchange rate of about 111 yen, the overall surplus was $4.24 billion and that with the United States $3.19 billion.
Private economists had estimated an overall trade surplus of between 396 billion yen and 650 billion yen against a 540.5 billion yen surplus a year ago and a 779.52 billion yen surplus in September.

The economists had expected a sharp pick-up in exports, especially car shipments to Asia and the United States, to help push up Japan's overall trade surplus in October as Japanese goods recovered global competitiveness with the weakening of the yen against the dollar.
A drop in the yen makes Japanese products cheaper in terms of foreign currency.
